Used by several basebords:

https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopenbmc%2Fentity-manager+path%3A%2F%5Econfigurations%5C%2F%2F+Status&type=code

Thanks, yes the `Status` is definitely used even outside `DisableNode`.

Reverted the change there and also in the other file. Please look again and let me know if it's good now 👍
Please answer in the commit message WHY we want to remove features, and we can go from there.

In my book any unused feature is fair game to remove from the community code.

Otherwise the code will just accumulate unused / broken / obsolete features over time and it will be harder to make changes going forward.


So me mentioning it as an unused feature is already plenty of justification.

It's intended to let you disable things downstream.  As an example, it lets you disable the "fan4" port, if you detect a chassis that only has 3 fans.

Lets get some justification for why we want to remove it, then we can go from there.  I suspect there's a simpler patch.

> As an example, it lets you disable the "fan4" port, if you detect a chassis that only has 3 fans.

I'm not sure how that would work. If you detected a chassis with 4 fans, it has 4 fans. If you detected a chassis with 3 fans, it has 3 fans.

Detecting one thing and then un-detecting it via another config seems misguided and the config is broken. We should detect the presence of things and not pretend something is there just to cancel it out via another config.

Just make 2 configs. One is the chassis config with 3 fans, another config for the chassis with 4 fans. Alternatively detect the fans as part of their own config.

> Lets get some justification for why we want to remove it,

In my book any unused feature is fair game to remove from the community code. As per the above reasoning there is no need for the feature and the use-case can be accomplished with 2 separate configs for the chassis variants.

> It could be there are people using this feature and we don't know about it.

I had a search through entire github 

https://github.com/search?q=%2F%28%3F-i%29%22DisableNode%22%2F+path%3A*.json&type=code&p=2

and there is no usage of this feature. We can speculate about hypothetical usage in private forks but with that mindset we will never be able to remove any feature, ever.

> > As an example, it lets you disable the "fan4" port, if you detect a chassis that only has 3 fans.
> 
> I'm not sure how that would work. If you detected a chassis with 4 fans, it has 4 fans. If you detected a chassis with 3 fans, it has 3 fans.

What if it matches neither chassis, or doesn't have a chassis?

> 
> Detecting one thing and then un-detecting it via another config seems misguided and the config is broken. We should detect the presence of things and not pretend something is there just to cancel it out via another config.

I can tell you that the intent works quite well, I'm not sure I'd call it "broken".  the goal is

1. The motherboard declares fan headers
2. The chassis declares fans

if no chassis is found, all the fan headers are enabled.  If a chassis is found, only the expected fan headers are enabled.  I have personally found this behavior useful, but I haven't no used it in several years.

> 
> Just make 2 configs. One is the chassis config with 3 fans, another config for the chassis with 4 fans. Alternatively detect the fans as part of their own config.
> 
> > Lets get some justification for why we want to remove it,
> 
> In my book any unused feature is fair game to remove

We VERY much disagree.  Just because it's not used by you, doesn't mean it's used by nobody.  Proving that nobody uses a feature is difficult, and especially for a small feature like this, isn't worth the maintenance effort to break by removal.  If we break it on accident, so be it, someone can send us the fix, but if we remove the feature entirely, it can prevent people upgrading that relied on it.

> from the community code. As per the above reasoning there is no need for the feature and the use-case can be accomplished with 2 separate configs for the chassis variants.

We disagree that this can be solved with 2 configs.  We also disagree that "there is no need".

> 
> > It could be there are people using this feature and we don't know about it.
> 
> I had a search through entire github 
> 
> https://github.com/search?q=%2F%28%3F-i%29%22DisableNode%22%2F+path%3A*.json&type=code&p=2
> 
> and there is no usage of this feature. We can speculate about hypothetical usage in private forks but with that mindset we will never be able to remove any feature, ever.

In my opinion you still haven't overcome the bar for "we should remove this", and considering I maintain this code, the maintenance burden partially falls on me.  I believe that randomly removing features based on a github search will be a larger maintenance burden than keeping them.

If this feature is preventing you from implementing something, I'm happy to have a technical discussion there about how to accomplish that, but the justification that nobody uses it therefore it's worth the effort to review and delete, I don't agree with.

> Proving that nobody uses a feature is difficult, and especially for a 
small feature like this, isn't worth the maintenance effort to break by 
removal. 

It's not 'difficult', it's *impossible*.

> If this feature is preventing you from implementing something, I'm happy
 to have a technical discussion there about how to accomplish that, but 
the justification that nobody uses it therefore it's worth the effort to
 review and delete, I don't agree with.

It's not 'preventing' me from doing anything, it is just slowing me down since i have to test the (likely) unused feature when making changes. So it's an ongoing burden for me, if it were to be removed, that is a one-time effort for you to review it and going forward things would be easier for me.

That being said, i guess it's up to you to decide which features to keep around.
